source: scene-timelines: per-frame traces of one cold boot per methodology on pokemon-speedrunning/gambatte-core, driven exactly as the Trainer-ID derivation harnesses drive it (tools/scene-timelines/scenes.cpp + analyze.py in RNG-Solution); scene edges are read off the emulator (frame luma, CPU PC/SP/stack, WRAM state), not counted

core.name: pokemon-speedrunning/gambatte-core
core.working_tree: the checkout at ~/gambatte-core is commit 5a41a68c plus ONE uncommitted compile-only line: libgambatte/src/mem/snes_spc/SNES_SPC.h line 1 "#include <cstdint>" (needed for GCC 13; no other tracked file differs - git status --short / git diff read at analysis time, below). The untracked files in the status are harness sources outside libgambatte/ and are not part of the build.
core.git_diff:
diff --git a/libgambatte/src/mem/snes_spc/SNES_SPC.h b/libgambatte/src/mem/snes_spc/SNES_SPC.h
index bd96a8f..9b1511b 100644
--- a/libgambatte/src/mem/snes_spc/SNES_SPC.h
+++ b/libgambatte/src/mem/snes_spc/SNES_SPC.h
@@ -1,3 +1,4 @@
+#include <cstdint>
 // SNES SPC-700 APU emulator
 
 // snes_spc 0.9.0
core.build_note: the harness (scenes.cpp, build line in SCENES.md) builds against the PRISTINE commit only with -include cstdint added to the g++ line: measured 2026-09-10 on a git-archive of 5a41a68c (GCC 13.3.0): without it the build fails with "libgambatte/src/mem/snes_spc/SNES_SPC.h:258:8: error: uint8_t does not name a type" (exit 1), with it the same command succeeds (exit 0)

frame_convention: 0-based harness frame index: frame f is the f-th runFor step of 35112 samples (70224 cycles) after power-on (on gba/gbp frame 0 includes gambatte's 485808-sample GBA->CGB stall); every frame number here is that index; scene ranges are [start, end) inclusive-exclusive; seconds = frame / (4194304/70224); every scene range AND the events flash_end / press_a_release are exclusive ends ([start, end): the frame at "end" is the first frame of the next scene), so the flash's last white frame = flash_end - 1 = flash_last_white
rom_note: the ROMs are the ones the tables were derived from (gen1-tid.json / gen2-tid.json sha1s; Red = ea9bcae6, the pret pokered build /mnt/hdd2/Red-WR-Practice/Red.gb that tidderive.cpp used). The header-renamed copies Blue.gb, Gold.gbc and Crystal.gbc in the untouched-ROMs folder never leave the boot ROM (header-checksum lock at PC 00ED / 00FA, measured), and Red.gb (98b130e2, title bytes only) reproduces pokered.gbc frame for frame (menu 1553 / 1701, same TIDs).
brightness_note: brightness[f] = mean Rec.601 luma (0-255) of the 160x144 frame after step f; DMG shades mapped to 255/170/85/0; CGB colours as gambatte-core renders them (the CGB boot ROM colourises Red/Blue/Yellow on gba/gbp/gbc)
flash_visible_note: Gen 1 events flash_visible_start / flash_last_white reproduce the TID guesser's white-frame rule (tidGuesserCore.js: a frame is white when at most 2 % of its pixels are dark, gray < 128 on the whole frame) from the trace's lmin column as lmin >= 128 (no pixel below 128 = 0 % dark, a subset of <= 2 %); the trace carries no dark-pixel fraction. Checked equal to the guesser's own screenDark <= 0.02 on its emulator fixtures (gba_358.csv / dmg_100.csv, same core): Red GBA white runs [1321,1390) and [1538,1601), Red DMG [1469,1538) and [1686,1749) under both rules; no frame in those ranges has 0 < screenDark <= 0.02. The "flash" scene itself keeps the strict all-white rule (lmin == 255): it starts 8 frames later, when the last light-grey pixels of the fade have gone.
scene_rules:
analyze.py -- turn the per-frame traces written by ./scenes (logs/<run>.csv) into scene-timelines.json.

Every frame number below is read off the trace (0-based harness frame index, see scenes.cpp); nothing is
computed from fixed counts.  Rules (all measured on the trace):
  W(f)  = every pixel white (lmin == 255); K(f) = every pixel black (lmax == 0); blank = W or K
  block = maximal run of consecutive blank / non-blank frames
  boot_logo      first non-white frame after power-on .. first all-white frame after it (boot ROM logo)
  game_init      first frame whose sampled PC is in the game's Init (boot ROM handed off)
  copyright      first non-blank block (>= 2 frames) after game_init
  Gen 1 gamefreak first non-blank block (>= 2 frames) after copyright ends (black bars + shooting star)
  Gen 1 intro    Red/Blue: first frame with a PlayIntroScene return address on the stack (bank $10);
                 Yellow: first frame with wYellowIntroCurrentScene != 0
  flash          the all-white block immediately before the title block (Red: the intro's white-out)
  title          the non-blank block immediately before the blank block that contains the menu detector
  skip           first frame of the blank block after the title (the title's START poll has been honoured);
                 Gen 2 also: first frame with SKIP_SPLASH_F (bit 6) set in wJumptableIndex (splash honours START)
  menu_open      the derivation harness's menu detector frame (Gen 1 wSaveFileStatus == 1; Gen 2 wMenuDataPointer)
  menu_visible   first non-blank frame after menu_open (the NEW GAME box is drawn)
  press_a        first frame with A down; roll = frame the IDs are written (Gen 1 wPlayerID != 0; Gen 2 wMoney == 3000)
  Gen 1 flash_visible_start / flash_last_white (the TID guesser's view of the flash, tidGuesserCore.js FLASH_DARK_MAX):
                 the guesser calls a frame white when at most 2 % of its pixels are dark (gray < 128 on the whole 160x144
                 frame, extractFeatures threshold 128). The trace has no dark-pixel fraction, only lmin/lmax/mean luma, so
                 the rule reproduced here is lmin >= 128 = NO pixel below the guesser's threshold = screenDark == 0, a
                 subset of "<= 2 %". flash_visible_start = first frame of the maximal lmin >= 128 run that contains the
                 strict all-white flash block (walk back from flash); flash_last_white = flash_end - 1 (the run's last
                 frame; the frame at flash_end has lmin < 128, asserted). Checked against the guesser's own per-frame
                 fixtures (hackmons-mobile tests/tid-guesser/fixtures/emu gba_358.csv / dmg_100.csv, screenDark from the
                 same core's frame dumps): over Red GBA frames 1200-1700 and Red DMG 1300-1850 the two rules select the
                 same frames (no frame has 0 < screenDark <= 0.02; the nearest is the menu's 0.048), so on these traces
                 the difference is nil. The "flash" scene keeps the strict all-white (lmin == 255) rule.

red/gba/hold-start-v1.input_pattern: cold boot, no input; START held from frame 1387 (window 1300-1475) until the NEW GAME menu detector (wSaveFileStatus == 1) fires on frame 1553, released from frame 1554; A held 8 frames from frame 1992 = menu_open + 1 + 80 (menu_to_table_frames) + offset 358 (the reference harness tidderive.cpp counts its 80-frame settle from the frame after the detection frame, so the data's "menu + 80 + offset" is this frame index minus 1); nothing else pressed.

events.roll_minus_press_note: roll - press_a at the single offset traced (offset_used 100 = crystal poll bin 23, offsets 98-101); it equals gen2-tid.json accept_to_roll_frames (14) only when offset_used is the last offset of its poll bin: the A-down is accepted at the bin's poll, 1 frame(s) after press_a, so the gap is 14 + 1 = 15 (Crystal offset 100 is bin 23 = offsets 98-101, hence 15 not 14)

free_run.note: no input at all (control): where the skipped/interrupted scenes fall when the game runs free

crystal/gbc/hold-start-v1.input_pattern: cold boot; START held from frame 203 (plateau 0-407) until the menu detector (wMenuDataPointer == MainMenu.MenuData) fires on frame 522, released from frame 523; A held 8 frames from frame 623 = menu_open + 1 + offset 100 (gen2-tid.json press_frame_rule); nothing else pressed; RTC day 0, clock running (gambatte cycle-based time, no setTime).
